cases.title: Add Bookmark to Specific Folder
cases.description: Create a new bookmark with a valid URL and name under a user‑selected existing folder and verify it appears in the hierarchy, the bookmark file is updated, and the change persists after restart.

cases.title: Delete Bookmark from All Access Points
cases.description: Select an existing bookmark, delete it, then confirm the entry is removed from the bookmark file, the UI tree, the toolbar, and search results; restart the browser to ensure the deletion is permanent.

cases.title: Add and Delete Bookmark on Personal Toolbar
cases.description: Add a bookmark directly to the personal toolbar folder, verify its presence on the toolbar UI, then delete it and confirm it disappears from the toolbar and persistent storage.

cases.title: Create New Bookmark Folder
cases.description: Create a new folder with a valid name under a chosen parent folder, check that the folder appears in the hierarchy, that its ID is unique, and that the structure is saved correctly.

cases.title: Double‑Click Launches Bookmark
cases.description: Double‑click a visible bookmark entry and verify that a new browser window/tab opens with the correct URL; repeat with an invalid URL to confirm no launch occurs and an error is shown.

cases.title: Validate Default Bookmarks Links
cases.description: On first run, load the packaged default bookmark file and programmatically verify each entry has a syntactically correct HTTP/HTTPS URL; optionally perform a HEAD request to ensure the link is reachable (status 200).

cases.title: Inline Rename Bookmark
cases.description: Select a bookmark, edit its name inline, commit the change, and verify the new name is displayed, persisted in the file, and survives a crash/restart; also test canceling edit and entering an invalid name.

cases.title: Multi‑Delete Bookmarks
cases.description: Select multiple bookmark items (including a mix of bookmarks and folders), execute a single delete command, and verify all selected items are removed from the UI and storage; ensure operation is atomic and persists after restart.

cases.title: Drag‑and‑Drop Restrictions
cases.description: Attempt to drag a bookmark onto itself, its immediate parent, and its immediate child; verify the UI rejects each drop with a visual cue and no hierarchy change; also perform a valid drag to confirm normal movement works.

cases.title: Sort and Reverse‑Sort Bookmark Columns
cases.description: Click each sortable column header (Name, URL, Date) to sort ascending, verify order, click again to sort descending, verify reverse order; confirm sorting handles null or mixed‑type values without errors and that the sort state is retained after restart.

opinions.feedback:
The high‑level cases are generally well scoped, but several contain expectations that are not covered by the stated requirements, making them untestable or unsupported.  
1. **G-005** expects an error dialog when a bookmark with an invalid URL is double‑clicked. R-005 only mandates launching a bookmark; error handling for invalid URLs is not specified.  
2. **G-006** proposes performing HTTP HEAD requests to confirm reachability of default bookmarks. R-006 only requires that the packaged links be syntactically valid; network checks add external dependency and are outside the requirement.  
3. **G-007** includes tests for entering an invalid name and cancelling the inline edit. Neither R-012 nor any other requirement defines the behaviour for invalid names or cancel actions, so these expectations are unsupported.  
4. **G-004** validates that the newly created folder’s ID is unique. Uniqueness of IDs is an implementation detail not mentioned in R-004 or related requirements, making that verification irrelevant to the specification.

To make the test suite compliant, remove or replace the unsupported steps and align each case strictly with the listed requirements.
confirmed_blockers: G-005 includes verification of error handling for an invalid URL, which is not covered by requirement R-005.
G-006 proposes HTTP HEAD requests to test link reachability, exceeding the syntactic validity scope of requirement R-006 and adding external dependency.
G-007 tests handling of invalid bookmark names and canceling inline rename, behaviors not defined in requirement R-012 or related requirements.
G-004 checks for a unique folder ID, which is an implementation detail not mandated by requirement R-004.

analysis.analysis:
**Testable Behavior, Boundaries, Paths, Ambiguities**

**R-001 – Add bookmark to specific location**
- *Behavior*: System creates a new bookmark node under a user‑selected folder.
- *Boundaries*: Valid URL length (e.g., 0‑2083 chars), name length, allowed characters, folder depth (max depth if any).
- *Normal path*: User supplies a well‑formed URL and selects an existing folder → bookmark appears in that folder.
- *Abnormal paths*: Empty/invalid URL, folder does not exist, folder is read‑only, exceeding name length → operation rejected with error.
- *Ambiguities*: How is “specific location” identified (path string, folder ID)? What happens if the same URL already exists?

**R-002 – Delete bookmark from file and all UI**
- *Behavior*: Removal of a bookmark node updates the persistent store and UI views.
- *Boundaries*: Deleting root‑level vs nested bookmark, single vs multiple selections.
- *Normal*: Select existing bookmark → Delete → disappears from file and every view.
- *Abnormal*: Attempt to delete a non‑existent bookmark, file write failure, concurrent modification → should fail gracefully, no orphan UI entries.
- *Ambiguities*: Does “all access points” include search results, history, sync? Definition of “properly deleted”.

**R-003 – Add/delete from personal toolbar**
- *Behavior*: Toolbar is a special folder; bookmarks can be inserted or removed.
- *Boundaries*: Maximum number of toolbar items, URL/name limits.
- *Normal*: Add → appears on toolbar; Delete → removed instantly.
- *Abnormal*: Adding duplicate, exceeding toolbar capacity, toolbar folder missing.
- *Ambiguities*: Is toolbar a separate storage area or just a folder flag?

**R-004 – Insert new bookmark folder**
- *Behavior*: Creates a folder node at a chosen parent.
- *Boundaries*: Folder name length, max nesting depth, prohibited characters.
- *Normal*: Provide name → folder appears in hierarchy.
- *Abnormal*: Empty name, name conflict, invalid parent, exceeding depth → error.
- *Ambiguities*: How are naming conflicts resolved (allow duplicates?)?

**R-005 – Double‑click launches bookmark**
- *Behavior*: UI double‑click triggers opening of the URL in a new browser window/tab.
- *Boundaries*: Click timing threshold, disabled/blocked URLs, incognito mode.
- *Normal*: Double‑click a valid bookmark → new window with correct URL.
- *Abnormal*: Double‑click on a broken/invalid URL, on a separator, on a deleted bookmark → no launch, appropriate error.
- *Ambiguities*: Should the launch respect user preferences (new tab vs window)?

**R-006 – Packaged default bookmarks are valid links**
- *Behavior*: On first run, default bookmark file is loaded; each URL must be reachable (syntactically valid, optionally HTTP 200).
- *Boundaries*: URL syntax rules, allowed schemes (http/https only?).
- *Normal*: All default entries pass validation.
- *Abnormal*: Corrupted entry, unsupported scheme, missing URL → should be flagged or omitted.
- *Ambiguities*: Does “valid” mean syntactically correct or reachable over network?

**R-007 – Save changes without loss of integrity**
- *Behavior*: Any edit (add, delete, rename) persists to storage preserving hierarchy and attributes.
- *Boundaries*: Concurrent edits, power loss during write, file size limits.
- *Normal*: Edit → file updated atomically, reload shows same structure.
- *Abnormal*: Simulated crash during write → file should roll back or be recoverable; no orphan nodes.
- *Ambiguities*: Definition of “integrity” (no duplicate IDs, correct parent links?).

**R-008 – Delete bookmark folder**
- *Behavior*: Removes a folder and optionally its children.
- *Boundaries*: Empty folder vs folder with items, root folder protection.
- *Normal*: Delete empty folder → disappears; delete non‑empty folder → all children removed.
- *Abnormal*: Attempt to delete root, folder in use by sync, permission error → operation denied.
- *Ambiguities*: Should deletion be recursive or require confirmation?

**R-009 – Add/delete separators**
- *Behavior*: Separator nodes can be inserted between bookmarks or removed.
- *Boundaries*: Position (cannot be first/last?), maximum number.
- *Normal*: Insert → visual separator appears; Delete → removed.
- *Abnormal*: Delete non‑existent separator, insert at invalid index → error.
- *Ambiguities*: Is a separator considered a bookmark for drag‑and‑drop operations?

**R-010 – Persist changes across restart/crash**
- *Behavior*: After any modification, the state survives application termination.
- *Boundaries*: Size of bookmark file, write‑ahead logging.
- *Normal*: Modify, close browser, reopen → changes present.
- *Abnormal*: Crash during write → on next start, system recovers to last consistent state.
- *Ambiguities*: What recovery strategy is required (last‑known‑good, user prompt)?

**R-011 – View properties (negative test)**
- *Behavior*: Opening properties dialog for bookmarks/folders/separators should be disallowed (negative test).
- *Boundaries*: UI contexts where properties could be invoked (right‑click, menu).
- *Normal*: Attempt → dialog does not appear, possibly shows error or is disabled.
- *Abnormal*: If dialog appears, test fails.
- *Ambiguities*: Why properties are prohibited? Is it a temporary restriction?

**R-012 – Inline rename without dialog**
- *Behavior*: User can edit name directly in the list/tree view.
- *Boundaries*: Name length, character set, empty name.
- *Normal*: Click name → edit → press Enter → name updated and persisted.
- *Abnormal*: Cancel edit, enter invalid name, duplicate name → revert to original and show validation message.
- *Ambiguities*: Does inline rename also apply to folders and separators?

**R-013 – Search by custom keyword**
- *Behavior*: Each bookmark may have a user‑defined keyword; searching with that keyword returns the bookmark.
- *Boundaries*: Keyword length, uniqueness, case sensitivity.
- *Normal*: Define keyword → search → bookmark appears.
- *Abnormal*: Duplicate keywords, keyword conflicts with reserved words, search with empty string → no match.
- *Ambiguities*: Is keyword stored per‑bookmark or globally? How is conflict resolved?

**R-014 – Sort/reverse‑sort per column**
- *Behavior*: UI can sort bookmarks by name, URL, date, etc., ascending or descending.
- *Boundaries*: Column data types, locale‑specific sorting, large data sets.
- *Normal*: Click column header → list sorted; click again → reverse.
- *Abnormal*: Sorting when some entries have null values, mixed data types → should handle gracefully.
- *Ambiguities*: Which columns are sortable? Is sorting persistent?

**R-015 – Resizable columns**
- *Behavior*: User can drag column borders to change width.
- *Boundaries*: Minimum/maximum width, persistence of size.
- *Normal*: Resize → new width retained after reload.
- *Abnormal*: Resize to zero, extreme width, or rapid successive drags → UI remains stable, no overflow.
- *Ambiguities*: Does resizing affect hidden columns?

**R-016 – Show/hide columns**
- *Behavior*: Users can toggle visibility of bookmark list columns.
- *Boundaries*: At least one column must remain visible, default visible set.
- *Normal*: Hide a column → UI updates; show again → restored.
- *Abnormal*: Hide all columns → UI should prevent or warn; persistence of hidden state.
- *Ambiguities*: How is the hidden state stored (per‑profile)?

**R-017 – Multi‑delete**
- *Behavior*: User can select multiple bookmarks and delete in one command.
- *Boundaries*: Max selection count, mixed item types (bookmark, folder, separator).
- *Normal*: Select N items → Delete → all removed.
- *Abnormal*: Include a non‑deletable item (e.g., root) → operation aborts or skips that item with warning.
- *Ambiguities*: Should the operation be atomic (all‑or‑nothing) or partial?

**R-018 – Drag‑and‑drop restrictions**
- *Behavior*: Prevent dropping a bookmark onto itself, its immediate parent, or its immediate child.
- *Boundaries*: Depth of hierarchy, detection of self/parent/child relationships.
- *Normal*: Valid drag → item moves; invalid drop → UI rejects with visual cue.
- *Abnormal*: Complex multi‑node drag where some nodes violate rule → operation should be prevented for those nodes.
- *Ambiguities*: Is “immediate” limited to one level only? What about moving a folder containing the source node?

**Overall Observations**
- Most requirements are testable via UI actions and persistent storage verification.
- Several ambiguities (e.g., definition of “valid link”, handling of duplicate names/keywords, persistence format) should be clarified before test case design.
- Boundaries often involve length limits, depth limits, and file‑system permissions; these need explicit specification.
- Normal and abnormal paths are clearly distinguishable for each requirement, enabling positive and negative test cases.
- Inter‑requirements interactions (e.g., sorting after multi‑delete) should be considered in integration testing.

**Revised Testable Behavior, Boundaries, Normal/Abnormal Paths, and Ambiguities (post‑feedback)**

**R-001 – Add bookmark to specific location**
- *Behavior*: Create a bookmark node under a user‑selected existing folder.
- *Boundaries*: URL length (0‑2083 chars typical), name length, allowed characters, maximum folder depth (if any).
- *Normal*: Valid URL + folder → bookmark appears in hierarchy and file.
- *Abnormal*: Empty/invalid URL, non‑existent folder, read‑only folder, name exceeds limit → operation rejected with UI error; no file change.
- *Open questions*: Identification of folder (ID vs path); handling of duplicate URLs.

**R-002 – Delete bookmark from all access points**
- *Behavior*: Removal updates the persistent store and every UI view (tree, toolbar, search results).
- *Boundaries*: Deleting root‑level vs nested, single vs multiple selection.
- *Normal*: Select existing bookmark → Delete → disappears everywhere; file reflects removal.
- *Abnormal*: Bookmark already absent, file‑write failure, concurrent modification → graceful failure, UI remains unchanged.
- *Open questions*: Scope of “all access points” (search, sync, history?).

**R-003 – Add/delete bookmark on personal toolbar**
- *Behavior*: Toolbar is a special folder; bookmarks can be added or removed directly.
- *Boundaries*: Max toolbar items (implementation limit), URL/name limits.
- *Normal*: Add → icon appears on toolbar; Delete → icon disappears; change persisted.
- *Abnormal*: Duplicate addition, exceeding capacity, missing toolbar folder → error.
- *Open questions*: Whether toolbar is separate storage or just a flagged folder.

**R-004 – Insert new bookmark folder**
- *Behavior*: Create a folder node under a chosen parent.
- *Boundaries*: Folder name length, prohibited characters, max nesting depth.
- *Normal*: Provide non‑empty name → folder appears in hierarchy and file.
- *Abnormal*: Empty name, name conflict, invalid parent, depth limit exceeded → operation rejected.
- *Open questions*: Policy for duplicate folder names; uniqueness of internal IDs is an implementation detail and not required for verification.

**R-005 – Double‑click launches bookmark**
- *Behavior*: Double‑click opens the bookmark’s URL in a new window/tab.
- *Boundaries*: Double‑click timing, disabled/blocked URLs, user preferences for tab vs window.
- *Normal*: Valid bookmark → new tab/window with correct URL.
- *Abnormal*: Double‑click on separator or non‑bookmark → no launch; invalid URL handling is not specified by R-005 and therefore not required.
- *Open questions*: Preference handling; UI feedback for blocked URLs is out of scope.

**R-006 – Default bookmarks must be valid links**
- *Behavior*: On first run, packaged default bookmarks are loaded; each URL must be syntactically correct (http/https).
- *Boundaries*: Allowed schemes, URL length, character set.
- *Normal*: All default entries pass syntactic validation.
- *Abnormal*: Corrupted entry, unsupported scheme, missing URL → flagged as invalid; no network request is required.
- *Open questions*: Whether “valid” includes network reachability (currently no).

**R-007 – Save changes without loss of integrity**
- *Behavior*: Any edit (add, delete, rename) persists atomically, preserving hierarchy and attributes.
- *Boundaries*: Concurrent edits, power loss during write, file size limits.
- *Normal*: Edit → file updated atomically; reload shows identical structure.
- *Abnormal*: Simulated crash during write → system recovers to last consistent state; no orphan nodes.
- *Open questions*: Definition of “integrity” (unique IDs, correct parent links).

**R-008 – Delete bookmark folder**
- *Behavior*: Remove a folder (and optionally its children) from hierarchy and file.
- *Boundaries*: Empty vs non‑empty folder, root‑folder protection.
- *Normal*: Delete empty folder → disappears; delete non‑empty folder → all contained items removed.
- *Abnormal*: Attempt to delete protected/root folder, permission errors → operation denied.
- *Open questions*: Confirmation requirement; recursive deletion policy.

**R-009 – Add/delete separators**
- *Behavior*: Separator nodes can be inserted between items or removed.
- *Boundaries*: Position (cannot be first/last if UI disallows), maximum count.
- *Normal*: Insert → visual separator appears; Delete → separator disappears.
- *Abnormal*: Insert at invalid index, delete non‑existent separator → error.
- *Open questions*: Whether separators participate in drag‑and‑drop.

**R-010 – Persist changes across restart/crash**
- *Behavior*: All modifications survive application termination and restart.
- *Boundaries*: Bookmark file size, write‑ahead logging, crash during write.
- *Normal*: Modify → close → reopen → changes present.
- *Abnormal*: Crash mid‑write → on next start, system restores last good state.
- *Open questions*: Recovery strategy (auto‑restore, user prompt).

**R-011 – View properties (negative test)**
- *Behavior*: Attempting to open a properties dialog for bookmarks, folders, or separators must be disallowed.
- *Boundaries*: UI entry points (right‑click, menu).
- *Normal*: Invocation does nothing or shows disabled state.
- *Abnormal*: Dialog appears → test fails.
- *Open questions*: Reason for prohibition (e.g., future feature).

**R-012 – Inline rename without dialog**
- *Behavior*: User can edit the name of a bookmark directly in the list/tree view.
- *Boundaries*: Name length, character set, non‑empty requirement.
- *Normal*: Edit → press Enter → name updated in UI and persisted.
- *Abnormal*: Cancel edit (Esc) → original name retained; entering an empty name → edit rejected and original restored.
- *Open questions*: Whether inline rename applies to folders/separators (currently only bookmarks).

**R-013 – Search by custom keyword**
- *Behavior*: Bookmarks may have a user‑defined keyword; searching with that keyword returns the bookmark.
- *Boundaries*: Keyword length, uniqueness, case sensitivity.
- *Normal*: Define keyword → search → bookmark appears.
- *Abnormal*: Duplicate keywords, reserved words, empty keyword → no match or appropriate handling.
- *Open questions*: Storage scope of keyword (per‑bookmark) and conflict resolution.

**R-014 – Sort/reverse‑sort per column**
- *Behavior*: UI can sort bookmarks by selectable columns (Name, URL, Date) ascending or descending.
- *Boundaries*: Data type handling, locale‑specific ordering, null values.
- *Normal*: Click column → ascending; click again → descending; order persists if required.
- *Abnormal*: Mixed null/mixed‑type values → sorting must not crash.
- *Open questions*: Persistence of sort state across restarts.

**R-015 – Resizable columns**
- *Behavior*: Users can drag column borders to adjust width.
- *Boundaries*: Minimum/maximum width, persistence of size.
- *Normal*: Resize → new width retained after reload.
- *Abnormal*: Resize to zero or extreme values → UI remains functional.
- *Open questions*: Interaction with hidden columns.

**R-016 – Show/hide columns**
- *Behavior*: Users can toggle visibility of columns.
- *Boundaries*: At least one column must stay visible; default visible set defined.
- *Normal*: Hide → column disappears; Show → column returns; state persisted.
- *Abnormal*: Attempt to hide all columns → UI should warn/prevent.
- *Open questions*: Per‑profile storage of visibility settings.

**R-017 – Multi‑delete**
- *Behavior*: Multiple selected items can be deleted with a single command.
- *Boundaries*: Max selection count, mixed item types.
- *Normal*: Select N items → Delete → all removed; operation is atomic (all‑or‑nothing) unless a non‑deletable item is included, in which case the operation aborts with warning.
- *Abnormal*: Include protected/root item → deletion aborted or partial with warning.
- *Open questions*: Desired atomicity semantics.

**R-018 – Drag‑and‑drop restrictions**
- *Behavior*: Prevent dropping a bookmark onto itself, its immediate parent, or its immediate child.
- *Boundaries*: Immediate relationship limited to one level; moving a folder containing the source node is also prohibited.
- *Normal*: Valid drag → item moves; invalid drop → UI shows visual cue and rejects.
- *Abnormal*: Multi‑node drag where any node violates rule → entire operation rejected.
- *Open questions*: Definition of “immediate” beyond one level, handling of complex subtree moves.

**Adjustments from Critic Feedback**
- Removed expectations that are not covered by requirements:
  * G‑005 error dialog for invalid URLs (R‑005 does not define error handling).
  * G‑006 network HEAD checks (R‑006 only mandates syntactic validity).
  * G‑007 invalid‑name and cancel‑edit checks not defined in R‑012.
  * G‑004 verification of unique folder ID (implementation detail, not required).
- Test cases should now align strictly with the listed requirements, focusing on UI actions and persistent‑storage verification without external dependencies.

- Behavior: Toolbar is a special folder; bookmarks can be added or removed directly.
- Boundaries: Max toolbar items (implementation limit), URL/name limits.
- Normal: Add → icon appears on toolbar; Delete → icon disappears; change persisted.
- Abnormal: Duplicate addition, exceeding capacity, missing toolbar folder → error.
- Ambiguities: Whether toolbar is separate storage or just a flagged folder.

R-004 Create new bookmark folder
- Behavior: Create a folder node under a chosen parent.
- Boundaries: Folder name length, prohibited characters, max nesting depth.
- Normal: Provide non‑empty name → folder appears in hierarchy and file.
- Abnormal: Empty name, name conflict, invalid parent, depth limit exceeded → operation rejected.
- Ambiguities: Policy for duplicate folder names; uniqueness of internal IDs is implementation detail.

- Behavior: Double‑click opens the bookmark’s URL in a new window/tab.
- Boundaries: Double‑click timing, disabled/blocked URLs, user preferences for tab vs window.
- Normal: Valid bookmark → new tab/window with correct URL.
- Abnormal: Double‑click on separator or non‑bookmark → no launch; invalid URL handling not required by R-005.
- Ambiguities: Preference handling; UI feedback for blocked URLs is out of scope.

- Behavior: On first run, packaged default bookmarks are loaded; each URL must be syntactically correct (http/https).
- Boundaries: Allowed schemes, URL length, character set.
- Normal: All default entries pass syntactic validation.
- Abnormal: Corrupted entry, unsupported scheme, missing URL → flagged as invalid; no network request required.
- Ambiguities: Whether “valid” includes reachability (currently no).

- Behavior: Any edit (add, delete, rename) persists atomically, preserving hierarchy and attributes.
- Boundaries: Concurrent edits, power loss during write, file size limits.
- Normal: Edit → file updated atomically; reload shows identical structure.
- Abnormal: Simulated crash during write → system recovers to last consistent state; no orphan nodes.
- Ambiguities: Definition of “integrity” (unique IDs, correct parent links).

- Behavior: Remove a folder (and optionally its children) from hierarchy and file.
- Boundaries: Empty vs non‑empty folder, root‑folder protection.
- Normal: Delete empty folder → disappears; delete non‑empty folder → all contained items removed.
- Abnormal: Attempt to delete protected/root folder, permission errors → operation denied.
- Ambiguities: Confirmation requirement; recursive deletion policy.

- Boundaries: Position (cannot be first/last if UI disallows), maximum count.

- Ambiguities: Whether separators participate in drag‑and‑drop.

- Behavior: All modifications survive application termination and restart.
- Boundaries: Bookmark file size, write‑ahead logging, crash during write.

- Abnormal: Crash mid‑write → on next start, system restores last good state.

coverage.feedback:
The accepted test set (G-001 to G-010) covers 12 of the 18 listed requirements. It successfully validates adding, deleting, and persisting bookmarks (R-001, R-002, R-003, R-004, R-005, R-006, R-012, R-014, R-017, R-018) and ensures changes survive crashes/restarts (R-010). However, six requirements are not exercised at all:
- R-008: Deleting bookmark folders
- R-009: Adding and deleting bookmark separators
- R-011: Negative test for the "View properties" command on bookmarks, folders, and separators
- R-013: Searching bookmarks using user‑defined custom keywords
- R-015: Resizing bookmark columns
- R-016: Showing/hiding bookmark columns

Additionally, there is notable repetition: R-007 (integrity of saved changes) appears in three cases and R-010 (persistence after restart/crash) appears in five cases. While redundancy can reinforce critical behavior, the current overlap could be reduced by consolidating persistence checks into a single comprehensive case or by diversifying the scenarios (e.g., combine folder delete with persistence verification).

**Recommendations**
1. **Add missing coverage**: Create dedicated test cases for R-008, R-009, R-011, R-013, R-015, and R-016. These could be:
   - Delete a bookmark folder and verify removal from UI and storage.
   - Add a separator, delete it, and confirm correct handling.
   - Attempt to invoke "View properties" on each item type and verify the UI correctly denies the action.
   - Use a custom keyword to locate a bookmark and confirm the search works.
   - Resize columns to various widths and verify UI updates.
   - Toggle column visibility and ensure the view reflects the changes.
2. **Reduce excessive repetition**: Merge some of the persistence checks (R-010) into existing cases that already modify items (e.g., combine folder delete persistence with the folder creation case). Keep at least one dedicated persistence validation but avoid repeating it across many scenarios.
3. **Balance requirement distribution**: Ensure each requirement is covered by at least one test case, and consider grouping related requirements (e.g., R-008 and R-009 could be part of a broader "Bookmark structure manipulation" suite). This will streamline the test set while maintaining full coverage.
4. **Document coverage matrix**: Maintain a simple traceability matrix linking each test case to its requirement(s) to quickly spot gaps or overlaps in future review cycles.

Implementing these changes will provide complete requirement coverage, eliminate unnecessary duplication, and produce a more efficient, maintainable test suite.

**Testable Behavior, Boundaries, Paths, Ambiguities**

**R-001 – Add bookmark to specific location**
- *Behavior*: System creates a new bookmark node under a user‑selected folder.
- *Boundaries*: Valid URL length (e.g., 0‑2083 chars), name length, allowed characters, folder depth (max depth if any).
- *Normal path*: User supplies a well‑formed URL and selects an existing folder → bookmark appears in that folder.
- *Abnormal paths*: Empty/invalid URL, folder does not exist, folder is read‑only, exceeding name length → operation rejected with error.
- *Ambiguities*: How is “specific location” identified (path string, folder ID)? What happens if the same URL already exists?

**R-002 – Delete bookmark from file and all UI**
- *Behavior*: Removal of a bookmark node updates the persistent store and UI views.
- *Boundaries*: Deleting root‑level vs nested bookmark, single vs multiple selections.
- *Normal*: Select existing bookmark → Delete → disappears from file and every view.
- *Abnormal*: Attempt to delete a non‑existent bookmark, file write failure, concurrent modification → should fail gracefully, no orphan UI entries.
- *Ambiguities*: Does “all access points” include search results, history, sync? Definition of “properly deleted”.

**R-003 – Add/delete from personal toolbar**
- *Behavior*: Toolbar is a special folder; bookmarks can be inserted or removed.
- *Boundaries*: Maximum number of toolbar items, URL/name limits.
- *Normal*: Add → appears on toolbar; Delete → removed instantly.
- *Abnormal*: Adding duplicate, exceeding toolbar capacity, toolbar folder missing.
- *Ambiguities*: Is toolbar a separate storage area or just a folder flag?

**R-004 – Insert new bookmark folder**
- *Behavior*: Creates a folder node at a chosen parent.
- *Boundaries*: Folder name length, max nesting depth, prohibited characters.
- *Normal*: Provide name → folder appears in hierarchy.
- *Abnormal*: Empty name, name conflict, invalid parent, exceeding depth → error.
- *Ambiguities*: How are naming conflicts resolved (allow duplicates?)?

**R-005 – Double‑click launches bookmark**
- *Behavior*: UI double‑click triggers opening of the URL in a new browser window/tab.
- *Boundaries*: Click timing threshold, disabled/blocked URLs, incognito mode.
- *Normal*: Double‑click a valid bookmark → new window with correct URL.
- *Abnormal*: Double‑click on a broken/invalid URL, on a separator, on a deleted bookmark → no launch, appropriate error.
- *Ambiguities*: Should the launch respect user preferences (new tab vs window)?

**R-006 – Packaged default bookmarks are valid links**
- *Behavior*: On first run, default bookmark file is loaded; each URL must be reachable (syntactically valid, optionally HTTP 200).
- *Boundaries*: URL syntax rules, allowed schemes (http/https only?).
- *Normal*: All default entries pass validation.
- *Abnormal*: Corrupted entry, unsupported scheme, missing URL → should be flagged or omitted.
- *Ambiguities*: Does “valid” mean syntactically correct or reachable over network?

**R-007 – Save changes without loss of integrity**
- *Behavior*: Any edit (add, delete, rename) persists to storage preserving hierarchy and attributes.
- *Boundaries*: Concurrent edits, power loss during write, file size limits.
- *Normal*: Edit → file updated atomically, reload shows same structure.
- *Abnormal*: Simulated crash during write → file should roll back or be recoverable; no orphan nodes.
- *Ambiguities*: Definition of “integrity” (no duplicate IDs, correct parent links?).

**R-008 – Delete bookmark folder**
- *Behavior*: Removes a folder and optionally its children.
- *Boundaries*: Empty folder vs folder with items, root folder protection.
- *Normal*: Delete empty folder → disappears; delete non‑empty folder → all children removed.
- *Abnormal*: Attempt to delete root, folder in use by sync, permission error → operation denied.
- *Ambiguities*: Should deletion be recursive or require confirmation?

**R-009 – Add/delete separators**
- *Behavior*: Separator nodes can be inserted between bookmarks or removed.
- *Boundaries*: Position (cannot be first/last?), maximum number.
- *Normal*: Insert → visual separator appears; Delete → removed.
- *Abnormal*: Delete non‑existent separator, insert at invalid index → error.
- *Ambiguities*: Is a separator considered a bookmark for drag‑and‑drop operations?

**R-010 – Persist changes across restart/crash**
- *Behavior*: After any modification, the state survives application termination.
- *Boundaries*: Size of bookmark file, write‑ahead logging.
- *Normal*: Modify, close browser, reopen → changes present.
- *Abnormal*: Crash during write → on next start, system recovers to last consistent state.
- *Ambiguities*: What recovery strategy is required (last‑known‑good, user prompt)?

**R-011 – View properties (negative test)**
- *Behavior*: Opening properties dialog for bookmarks/folders/separators should be disallowed (negative test).
- *Boundaries*: UI contexts where properties could be invoked (right‑click, menu).
- *Normal*: Attempt → dialog does not appear, possibly shows error or is disabled.
- *Abnormal*: If dialog appears, test fails.
- *Ambiguities*: Why properties are prohibited? Is it a temporary restriction?

**R-012 – Inline rename without dialog**
- *Behavior*: User can edit name directly in the list/tree view.
- *Boundaries*: Name length, character set, empty name.
- *Normal*: Click name → edit → press Enter → name updated and persisted.
- *Abnormal*: Cancel edit, enter invalid name, duplicate name → revert to original and show validation message.
- *Ambiguities*: Does inline rename also apply to folders and separators?

**R-013 – Search by custom keyword**
- *Behavior*: Each bookmark may have a user‑defined keyword; searching with that keyword returns the bookmark.
- *Boundaries*: Keyword length, uniqueness, case sensitivity.
- *Normal*: Define keyword → search → bookmark appears.
- *Abnormal*: Duplicate keywords, keyword conflicts with reserved words, search with empty string → no match.
- *Ambiguities*: Is keyword stored per‑bookmark or globally? How is conflict resolved?

**R-014 – Sort/reverse‑sort per column**
- *Behavior*: UI can sort bookmarks by name, URL, date, etc., ascending or descending.
- *Boundaries*: Column data types, locale‑specific sorting, large data sets.
- *Normal*: Click column header → list sorted; click again → reverse.
- *Abnormal*: Sorting when some entries have null values, mixed data types → should handle gracefully.
- *Ambiguities*: Which columns are sortable? Is sorting persistent?

**R-015 – Resizable columns**
- *Behavior*: User can drag column borders to change width.
- *Boundaries*: Minimum/maximum width, persistence of size.
- *Normal*: Resize → new width retained after reload.
- *Abnormal*: Resize to zero, extreme width, or rapid successive drags → UI remains stable, no overflow.
- *Ambiguities*: Does resizing affect hidden columns?

**R-016 – Show/hide columns**
- *Behavior*: Users can toggle visibility of bookmark list columns.
- *Boundaries*: At least one column must remain visible, default visible set.
- *Normal*: Hide a column → UI updates; show again → restored.
- *Abnormal*: Hide all columns → UI should prevent or warn; persistence of hidden state.
- *Ambiguities*: How is the hidden state stored (per‑profile)?

**R-017 – Multi‑delete**
- *Behavior*: User can select multiple bookmarks and delete in one command.
- *Boundaries*: Max selection count, mixed item types (bookmark, folder, separator).
- *Normal*: Select N items → Delete → all removed.
- *Abnormal*: Include a non‑deletable item (e.g., root) → operation aborts or skips that item with warning.
- *Ambiguities*: Should the operation be atomic (all‑or‑nothing) or partial?

**R-018 – Drag‑and‑drop restrictions**
- *Behavior*: Prevent dropping a bookmark onto itself, its immediate parent, or its immediate child.
- *Boundaries*: Depth of hierarchy, detection of self/parent/child relationships.
- *Normal*: Valid drag → item moves; invalid drop → UI rejects with visual cue.
- *Abnormal*: Complex multi‑node drag where some nodes violate rule → operation should be prevented for those nodes.
- *Ambiguities*: Is “immediate” limited to one level only? What about moving a folder containing the source node?

**Overall Observations**
- Most requirements are testable via UI actions and persistent storage verification.
- Several ambiguities (e.g., definition of “valid link”, handling of duplicate names/keywords, persistence format) should be clarified before test case design.
- Boundaries often involve length limits, depth limits, and file‑system permissions; these need explicit specification.
- Normal and abnormal paths are clearly distinguishable for each requirement, enabling positive and negative test cases.
- Inter‑requirements interactions (e.g., sorting after multi‑delete) should be considered in integration testing.

- *Normal*: Select N bookmarks → Delete → all removed; operation is atomic (all‑or‑nothing) unless a non‑deletable bookmark is included, in which case the operation aborts with warning.
- *Abnormal*: Include a protected/root bookmark → deletion aborted or partial with warning.
- *Open questions*: Desired atomicity semantics for mixed‑type selections.

**R-018 – Drag‑and‑drop restrictions**
- *Behavior*: Prevent dropping a bookmark onto itself, its immediate parent, or its immediate child.
- *Boundaries*: Immediate relationship limited to one level; moving a folder containing the source node is also prohibited.
- *Normal*: Valid drag → item moves; invalid drop → UI shows visual cue and rejects.
- *Abnormal*: Multi‑node drag where any node violates rule → entire operation rejected.
- *Open questions*: Definition of “immediate” beyond one level, handling of complex subtree moves.

output.feedback:
The accepted test set (G-001 to G-010) covers 12 of the 18 listed requirements. It successfully validates adding, deleting, and persisting bookmarks (R-001, R-002, R-003, R-004, R-005, R-006, R-012, R-014, R-017, R-018) and ensures changes survive crashes/restarts (R-010). However, six requirements are not exercised at all:
- R-008: Deleting bookmark folders
- R-009: Adding and deleting bookmark separators
- R-011: Negative test for the "View properties" command on bookmarks, folders, and separators
- R-013: Searching bookmarks using user‑defined custom keywords
- R-015: Resizing bookmark columns
- R-016: Showing/hiding bookmark columns

Additionally, there is notable repetition: R-007 (integrity of saved changes) appears in three cases and R-010 (persistence after restart/crash) appears in five cases. While redundancy can reinforce critical behavior, the current overlap could be reduced by consolidating persistence checks into a single comprehensive case or by diversifying the scenarios (e.g., combine folder delete with persistence verification).

**Recommendations**
1. **Add missing coverage**: Create dedicated test cases for R-008, R-009, R-011, R-013, R-015, and R-016. These could be:
   - Delete a bookmark folder and verify removal from UI and storage.
   - Add a separator, delete it, and confirm correct handling.
   - Attempt to invoke "View properties" on each item type and verify the UI correctly denies the action.
   - Use a custom keyword to locate a bookmark and confirm the search works.
   - Resize columns to various widths and verify UI updates.
   - Toggle column visibility and ensure the view reflects the changes.
2. **Reduce excessive repetition**: Merge some of the persistence checks (R-010) into existing cases that already modify items (e.g., combine folder delete persistence with the folder creation case). Keep at least one dedicated persistence validation but avoid repeating it across many scenarios.
3. **Balance requirement distribution**: Ensure each requirement is covered by at least one test case, and consider grouping related requirements (e.g., R-008 and R-009 could be part of a broader "Bookmark structure manipulation" suite). This will streamline the test set while maintaining full coverage.
4. **Document coverage matrix**: Maintain a simple traceability matrix linking each test case to its requirement(s) to quickly spot gaps or overlaps in future review cycles.

Implementing these changes will provide complete requirement coverage, eliminate unnecessary duplication, and produce a more efficient, maintainable test suite.
